title: GMLake: Efficient and Transparent GPU Memory Defragmentation for Large-scale DNN Training with Virtual Memory Stitching
problem: GPU memory allocators using caching with splitting mechanisms suffer from severe fragmentation when memory reduction techniques (re-computation, offloading, distributed training, low-rank adaptation) introduce frequent and irregular memory allocation/deallocation requests. This fragmentation wastes precious GPU memory capacity, a critical bottleneck for training large language models.
motivation: GPU memory capacity is a fundamental constraint for training resource-intensive large-scale DNNs and LLMs, and memory fragmentation significantly reduces the effective memory available for these critical AI workloads.
method: GMLake leverages low-level GPU virtual memory management with a novel virtual memory stitching (VMS) mechanism that fuses non-contiguous physical memory blocks through virtual address mapping. The framework intercepts memory allocation/deallocation requests and transparently remaps fragmented physical memory into contiguous virtual address spaces, eliminating fragmentation without modifying DNN models or memory reduction techniques.
key_novelty: Virtual memory stitching mechanism that enables combining non-contiguous physical GPU memory blocks into a contiguous virtual address space through GPU virtual memory management, eliminating fragmentation transparently.
contributions: Novel GPU memory allocation framework (GMLake) based on virtual memory management that addresses fragmentation from memory reduction techniques
Virtual memory stitching (VMS) mechanism for transparently fusing non-contiguous memory blocks
Demonstrated significant memory savings on large language models with 9.2 GB average reduction and up to 25 GB peak reduction
Transparent integration ensuring seamless execution without modifying DNN frameworks or memory reduction techniques

metrics.other: 9.2 GB average memory reduction (up to 25 GB), 15% average fragmentation reduction (up to 33%)

primary_theme: GPU memory fragmentation mitigation through virtual memory stitching
